items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: Also in the same band was a fine guitar player... And, of course, let me see. There was a bass player in there, Quinn Wilson.

ctx.x: Also in the same band was a fine guitar player. He's passed away since. Lawrence Dixon was his name. And we had another fine trumpet player who doubled on alto saxophone, George Dixon. He was another fine man in that band. And, of course, there were three of us trombone players and I mentioned previously that two of these guys have passed away now. And that would be Billy Franklin and Louis Taylor.

And, of course, let me see. There was a bass player in there, Quinn Wilson. He did -- he was a good arranger. We call him Cupie. And he did quite a bit of writing for Earl back in those days. And he played a string bass and he also played a tuba. And he was a wonderful soloist on tuba, and Earl featured him quite a bit.

So, I don't know, that was a fast resume of the guys in the band with Earl. And, of course, as I mentioned previously that the guy I was more close to in that band was Ray Nance. And the reason I remember him so well was Ray was a fine musician and he had his own little group before he came with Earl. He had a fine little group and they were all youngsters playing around Chicago. And Ray always was a fine violinist. I think he played violin before he did trumpet.

items.title: 70980_Quinn Wilson oral history interview
items.q: That's the same nightclub we found Bill Eckstein.* Also Trummy Young.

ctx.x: Where did he find all these very talented guys?
Jimmy Mundy we found in the Crystal Caverns in Washington, D. C. That's the same nightclub we found Bill Eckstein.* Also Trummy Young.
